cards.headline: 2,520 BTO flats with waits of around three years to go on sale in June
bullets: 2,520 new HDB flats with waits of about three years will be available in June.
Two projects in Sembawang offer shorter waits of under three years.
The Ang Mo Kio project has a wait of just over three years.
New amenities like childcare and minimarts will be ready soon after residents move in.

cards.headline: 28 HDB projects could get new refuse chute doors to prevent dumping of bulky items
bullets: 28 HDB blocks might get new rubbish chute doors to stop bulky item dumping.
New chute doors have smaller openings to prevent blockages from large items.
This aims to fix problems caused by items like boxes and renovation waste.
HDB will first test the new doors in three projects starting late 2026.

cards.headline: Family of late Creative Technology founder Sim Wong Hoo donates $385,000 to ST pocket money fund
bullets: Sim Wong Hoo's family gave $385,000 to the ST School Pocket Money Fund.
The donation marked the launch of a book about the late Creative Technology founder.
Sim Wong Hoo founded the well-known home-grown company Creative Technology in 1981.
His nephew presented the cheque, continuing his legacy of helping students.

cards.headline: 87-year-old driver among 3 taken to hospital after accident in Queenstown carpark
bullets: Three people, including an 87-year-old driver, went to hospital after a crash in Queenstown.
The accident happened in a Ghim Moh Road carpark involving three cars and a pedestrian.
Police were called to the scene around 5.20pm on June 6.
Investigations into the incident are still ongoing.

cards.headline: Motorcyclist dies in hospital after accident in Yishun
bullets: A 36-year-old motorcyclist died after his vehicle skidded in Yishun on June 3.
The accident happened on Yishun Avenue 1 towards Mandai Avenue around 9.15am.
The motorcyclist was taken to Khoo Teck Puat Hospital where he later passed away.
Police are investigating the incident.

cards.headline: Over 2,500 flats with wait times of around 3 years or less to be offered in June BTO exercise
bullets: About 2,520 HDB flats with wait times of three years or less will be offered in June.
These flats are in Sembawang and Ang Mo Kio.
They make up over a third of the 6,900 flats launching next month.
Two Sembawang projects have wait times under three years.
The Ang Mo Kio project has a wait time of just over three years.

cards.headline: Two Singapore residents who were on hantavirus-hit cruise ship complete quarantine
bullets: Two Singapore residents who were on a cruise ship with a hantavirus outbreak have finished their quarantine.
They both tested negative for the virus before being released.
The two men arrived in Singapore in early May and were isolated.
Hantavirus is carried by rodents and can cause serious illness.

cards.headline: Olinda Cho recovers from lyric slip-up in Midlife, Sing & Shine! 4 to make Top 14
bullets: Olinda Cho made it to the Top 14 in a Hong Kong singing show.
She sang a Cantonese song but forgot some lyrics mid-performance.
Cho recovered well and finished the song, impressing viewers.
She spent a month learning the song and Cantonese pronunciation.

cards.headline: Luxury yacht catches fire at Sentosa Cove marina
bullets: A luxury yacht called Eagle Wings III caught fire at Sentosa Cove marina.
Thick black smoke was seen coming from the burning yacht.
The Singapore Civil Defence Force responded quickly to put out the fire.
No injuries were reported from the incident.
The yacht was later seen partially submerged in the water.

cards.headline: Snark subreddits: Why do we spend so much time on people and things we cannot stand?
bullets: Online groups called snark subreddits let people criticise celebrities and influencers.
These communities allow users to gossip, mock, and dissect public figures.
Some join these spaces out of boredom, loneliness, or frustration.
They offer a place to share opinions that might be rejected elsewhere.
Many find comfort in connecting with others who dislike the same things.

cards.headline: The Albanian island at the centre of anger over Kushner’s resort plans
bullets: Protests erupted in Albania after a security guard allegedly injured a protester at a resort site.
Plans by Jared Kushner to build a luxury resort on the island of Sazan have angered environmentalists.
The island, a former military base, is part of Albania's only marine national park.
Critics say the government approved the projects without enough transparency, favouring investors.
The prime minister insists the projects will proceed, calling them vital for economic progress.

cards.headline: England’s World Cup opener is set to cause power spike
bullets: England's World Cup opener could cause a big jump in power use.
Kettles boiling at half-time are expected to cause the biggest surge.
Power demand might rise by 800 megawatts during the match.
Britain now uses mostly wind and solar power, not coal.
Football-related power spikes are common across Europe.

cards.headline: Jaecoo 8 review: a three-row SUV that excels at one thing
bullets: The Jaecoo 8 SUV can travel up to 1,200 km on a full tank, meaning fewer refuels.
This plug-in hybrid SUV offers 134 km of electric-only driving before the engine kicks in.
It boasts 428 horsepower and can accelerate from 0 to 100 kmh in 5.8 seconds.
The cabin feels luxurious with features like massage seats and a premium sound system.
However, the third-row seats are very cramped for adults, making it a 5+2 seater.

cards.headline: URA lifts ban on new hotels, hostels and serviced apartments in Boat Quay, Beach Road areas
bullets: New hotels, hostels, and serviced apartments can now be built in Boat Quay and Beach Road.
The government is testing new ways to use city spaces to make the downtown area livelier.
Rules on how spaces can be used will be relaxed in some areas to try out new ideas.
These changes aim to give visitors more places to stay and boost local businesses.

cards.headline: Hong Kong’s second-largest hotel risks being seized by banks
bullets: Banks want to take over a 1,200-room Sheraton hotel in Hong Kong due to a defaulted loan.
The hotel owner, Shimao Group, owes banks S$737 million.
The hotel is the second-largest in Hong Kong by room count.
Banks are increasingly taking over properties to recover bad debts.

cards.headline: Someone to share stories with: M'sian woman, 66, marries late sister's husband, 72, 6 years after losing her own
bullets: A 66-year-old woman married her late sister's husband, 72, on May 30.
The idea came from her brother who saw the widower was sad.
Both families agreed to the marriage after discussions.
The couple sought companionship and someone to share life with.
The wedding footage shared online received mixed reactions.

cards.headline: DJ Hazelle Teo, 32, marries S'pore-based musician James Wong, 26, cuts hair mid-ceremony
bullets: DJ Hazelle Teo, 32, married musician James Wong, 26, in a ceremony.
The couple met during a work collaboration and announced their engagement last year.
Hazelle Teo also cut her hair during the wedding festivities.
They playfully tricked guests with a fake pregnancy announcement.

cards.headline: S'pore man, 32, allegedly crashes car into Yishun void deck, flees & locks himself inside unit for around 4 hours
bullets: A 32-year-old man crashed his car into a Yishun void deck and fled.
Police found a stun device and drug items in the car.
The man locked himself in a flat for four hours before being arrested.
He faces charges for the stun device, traffic offences, and suspected drug offences.

cards.headline: There’s A Toy Sale At HomeTeamNS Khatib With Up To 90% Off & Free Mascot Meet & Greets
bullets: Toy Fiesta sale at HomeTeamNS Khatib offers up to 90% off popular toys.
Prices start from $1 for items like Hot Wheels and baby toys.
You can find toys from brands like Pokémon, Sanrio, Marvel, and Frozen.
Free mascot meet and greets are available for Robocar Poli and Amber.
The sale runs until June 7th and is a short walk from Khatib MRT.

cards.headline: There’s A LEGO x FIFA World Cup Pop-Up At Compass One, With Interactive Activities & Free Mini LEGO Sets
bullets: A LEGO FIFA World Cup pop-up is happening at Compass One until June 21, 2026.
You can complete activities to win free mini LEGO sets or vouchers.
Take photos with LEGO football stars and build your own custom jersey.
There are games like Brick Dribble and LEGO Robo Striker Arena to play.
Exclusive LEGO World Cup sets and special deals are available for purchase.

cards.headline: McDonald’s Has FIFA-Themed Collectible Cups & Happy Meal Toys, Plus A Finals Watch Party
bullets: McDonald's is releasing FIFA World Cup themed meals and collectible cups starting June 11th.
Kids can get Squishmallows football toys with Happy Meals, with new ones weekly.
Redeem a McDonald's football kit with 3,000 app points from June 29th.
Watch the FIFA World Cup Finals live at McDonald's Marine Cove on July 20th.
The Finals Watch Party includes unlimited McNuggets and fries for attendees.
